content.title: About
content.content: Bananas are elongated, soft, sweet fruits that grow in hanging clusters on large herbaceous plants of the genus Musa, native to Southeast Asia. They have a thick peel that turns from green to yellow as they ripen and a creamy flesh. Bananas are one of the most widely eaten fruits in the world and are enjoyed fresh, in desserts, smoothies, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Botanically, a banana is a berry, and the plant it grows on is a giant herb, not a tree.
A cluster of bananas is called a hand, and each individual banana is called a finger.
The Cavendish variety is the most widely exported banana.
As bananas ripen, starch turns into sugar, which is why ripe bananas taste sweeter.
Plantains are a starchier type of banana usually eaten cooked.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Bananas are a well-known source of potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports normal metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C and manganese
items.content: These nutrients support the immune system and normal metabolism.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Bananas contribute fiber, and less ripe bananas contain resistant starch, which supports digestion.

items.title: Quick, convenient energy
items.content: Bananas are an easy source of carbohydrates before or after activity.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Ripe bananas contain natural sugars, so portions matter for people monitoring blood sugar.

items.title: Potassium considerations
items.content: People with kidney problems or those taking certain medications, such as some blood pressure drugs, should consult a healthcare professional about potassium intake.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people, especially those with latex allergy, may react to bananas.

items.title: Digestive effects
items.content: Unripe bananas may cause constipation or bloating in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bananas can be eaten fresh, sliced onto oatmeal, cereal, or yogurt, or blended into smoothies. Very ripe bananas are good for banana bread, pancakes, and desserts. They can also be baked, grilled, or frozen for ice-cream-like treats.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bananas at room temperature until ripe. To slow ripening, separate the bunch and keep them away from other ripening fruit. The peel turns dark in the refrigerator, but the flesh is usually still fine. Ripe bananas can be peeled and frozen for smoothies and baking.
